overview: Norway is a country in northern Europe, on the western side of the Scandinavian peninsula. Its capital and largest city is Oslo. Norway is a constitutional monarchy and became fully independent from Sweden in 1905. It is not a member of the European Union. Oil and gas from under the North Sea have made it one of the richest countries in the world.

geography.text: Norway is long, narrow and mountainous, with a deeply cut coastline of fjords carved by glaciers. Thousands of islands lie off the coast, and in the far north, beyond the Arctic Circle, the sun does not set in midsummer. The Svalbard islands, far out in the Arctic Ocean, are also part of Norway.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Mild on the coast thanks to the Gulf Stream, but cold and snowy inland and in the north.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Reindeer, moose, musk oxen and polar bears on Svalbard; orcas and whales feed off the coast.

history.text: Norwegian Vikings sailed as far as Iceland, Greenland and North America. Norway was united as a kingdom around the 900s, but from 1380 it was joined with Denmark, and from 1814 with Sweden. It became fully independent in 1905. Occupied by Germany in the Second World War, Norway later grew rich from North Sea oil, discovered in 1969.

events.title: Vikings in America
events.text: Leif Erikson reaches North America, around 500 years before Columbus.

events.title: Constitution
events.text: Norway adopts a constitution, then enters a union with Sweden.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Norway peacefully ends its union with Sweden.

events.title: German invasion
events.text: Germany occupies Norway for five years.

events.title: Oil discovered
events.text: Oil is found under the North Sea, transforming the economy.

government.text: Norway is a constitutional monarchy. The King is head of state and the Prime Minister leads the government, which must have the support of the Storting, the parliament. Norway is a founding member of NATO but has voted twice, in 1972 and 1994, not to join the European Union.

economy.text: Oil and gas from the North Sea made Norway one of the richest countries in the world. The government saves much of the money in the world's largest sovereign wealth fund, worth more than all of Norway's yearly economy many times over. Fishing, salmon farming and shipping are also big industries, and almost all of its electricity comes from hydropower.

culture.text: Norway's landscape of fjords and mountains shaped its culture and folk tales of trolls. The painter Edvard Munch made The Scream, and the playwright Henrik Ibsen wrote A Doll's House. The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo every year.

items.title: Fjords
items.text: Long, deep sea inlets carved by glaciers, such as Geirangerfjord.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Salmon, cod and brown cheese, brunost, with a sweet caramel taste.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Norway gave the world Ibsen's plays, Munch's paintings and Grieg's music.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: On Constitution Day, 17 May, children march through towns waving flags, and many people wear traditional bunad costumes.

sport.text: Norway is the most successful country in the history of the Winter Olympics, with a huge medal haul in cross-country skiing and biathlon. Footballer Erling Haaland is one of the best strikers in the world.

items.title: Winter Olympics
items.text: More medals than any other country in history.
Oslo and Lillehammer hosted the Winter Olympics.

didYouKnow: Norway introduced salmon sushi to Japan in the 1980s.
In parts of northern Norway, the sun doesn't set for weeks in summer.

keyPeople.name: Roald Amundsen
keyPeople.text: Led the first expedition to reach the South Pole, in 1911.

keyPeople.name: Erling Haaland
keyPeople.text: Set the Premier League record for goals in a season.
